summary: The drop-down Terminal is a real terminal on X: xterm embedded with -into, running the owner's configured shell in the Files folder. Under Xvfb it was tested with a key read, tty, top and q, a vim edit saved, and dir with its Debian line. B4's behaviour is kept: the keys, the slide, Put away, and the keys going back. Win+`, Ctrl+Alt+T and Ctrl+Alt+` are grabbed on the drop-down's own window, so they work inside vim. Exit puts it away. For bash, DOS words come from a Graphite rc that reads ~/.bashrc first (the owner's files are untouched) and then binds Enter. The rc shows W1's 'dir → ls -l' in place of the typed line, and the Debian command runs and stays in history. Off X, or without xterm, B4's line Terminal stays.

added: tests_integrated/test_real_terminal.py: 7 under its own Xvfb, driven by real XTest keys (real terminal, key read, top+q, vim saves, dir Debian line, Win+` hides and the keys go back, a bar row is typed in and exit puts it away); 1 for bash with the rc in a pty (dir shown, the alias and PS1 from ~/.bashrc kept, the Debian command in history, ~/.bashrc unchanged); 5 pure

decisions: Design (a): xterm -into. It is far less code than a pty and VT emulator, it is a proven terminal, and xterm is already in graphite-session's Depends (PK1). No pyte.

DOS words: bash's Enter is bound (bind -x macro, emacs and vi-insert) to ask the translator about the raw line. Only lines whose first word is a DOS word or drive letter reach Python. The translator is W1's translate, so backslashes and drive letters arrive intact. Shown: 'dir → ls -l' (dim) replaces the typed line; the shell line then shows and runs the Debian command, and Up brings that back. A shell other than bash runs as is, with the header saying 'DOS words need bash'.

del and erase run 'gio trash' (the freedesktop bin, never rm), and *.* asks y/N first. The 1.0 line Terminal used the Kernel's files.batch with an Undo link; the real shell cannot reach the Kernel. libglib2.0-bin was added for gio.

The bar's Terminal and DOS rows (the owner's press) are queued in Graphite's own folder (XDG_RUNTIME_DIR/graphite-terminal, 0700) and taken in with one XTest key (Ctrl+Alt+Shift+F12, bound by the rc), but only while the shell is at its prompt (checked through /proc tpgid). While a program runs there, the line is not typed and the header says the Terminal is busy.

The hide keys are XGrabKey'd on the drop-down's toplevel while it is down, so they reach Graphite even inside vim. They are also polled on an 80 ms timer, because Xlib can queue events off the socket.

The look: -bg TERMINAL_GROUND, -fg the cue words (as B4), sixteen colours for a light or dark ground. IBM Plex Mono comes from Graphite's branding/fonts/plex through a FONTCONFIG_FILE for xterm only; the rc unsets it for the shell. Ctrl+Shift+C and V copy and paste.

Worktree: the original worktree was removed while I was paused. I worked in a scratch clone of 29778a8 and nothing in /home/user/Struthio was touched. The patch applies to 29778a8 and, with -3, to 994da40.
findings_for_the_coordinator: Nothing ran on the owner's ThinkPad or under real Fluxbox. The tests used Xvfb with no window manager, and the frames were taken without a window manager or the bar.
sudo's password prompt was not shown: the container runs as root, so sudo never asks. tty in the drop-down names /dev/pts/N (tested), so the prompt should work, but that is unverified.
The look is read when xterm starts. After a look change, the open shell keeps its colours until it exits and the next drop starts a new one.

The X tests need Xvfb, xterm, vim, top and Qt's xcb platform. In this container that means LD_LIBRARY_PATH to b100/S3/xcblibs; without it the class skips and names the missing piece. The tier wrapper must pass that variable for the X tests to run.
1.0's in-window Terminal and Kas's paths are unchanged. Only DropTerminal.run, which is reached from the owner's bar rows, types into the real shell.

release_note: A real Terminal. The Terminal that drops from the top of the screen (Win+` or Ctrl+Alt+T) is now a real terminal running your own shell, so vim, top, less, ssh and sudo's password prompt work in it. Your own ~/.bashrc is read and never changed. DOS words still work: type dir and it shows 'dir → ls -l', then runs ls -l (Up brings back the Debian command). del puts files in the bin. The same key, or exit, puts it away, and the app you were in gets the keys back. Ctrl+Shift+C and Ctrl+Shift+V copy and paste.
